findings.claim: The last equality check before the charge write covers only the execution-ledger source and named native sequences, not every P14 input re-hashed into the immediately preceding boundary receipt.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Immediately before the guarded write, re-read the source hash/version and all boundary-bound native invalidation/authority/revocation/Goal/Team/capability sequences and require exact equality to the receipt
findings.impact: A WBS, dependency, design/source, AIP/ASC, or budget input can change after the boundary receipt but before the ledger write without triggering the specified final comparison, so an attempt can be charged against stale admission evidence outside the disclosed post-comparison TOCTOU window.
findings.recommended_action: Require the guarded writer to re-hash or revalidate every P14/P1-P16 input, or one aggregate identity covering all of them, immediately before the write; abort with no ledger write on any mismatch and bind the complete check set into the write receipt.

findings.claim: The ordinary APPLIED completion rule does not require or reference the GuardedWriteReceipt that is mandatory only for candidate-equal recovery finalization.
findings.evidence_excerpt: A create-once `ExecutionTransitionCompletion` binds the intent plus observed persisted hash and validator results as `APPLIED`
findings.impact: Exact candidate bytes written manually or through an unguarded path can be strict-validated and given an APPLIED completion, after which P3 can treat the lineage as valid without persisted proof that the authorized writer executed the version, boundary, and authority checks; this can legitimize a stale charge or acceptance projection.
findings.recommended_action: Make one hash-bound GuardedWriteReceipt from the exact P15-bound writer mandatory for every APPLIED completion and P3 lineage link, not only recovery finalization, and reject absent or mismatched receipt references.

findings.claim: A source-equal charge restart must persist a NOT_APPLIED completion even though the exhaustive Section 5.1 pre-charge write set does not include an ExecutionTransitionCompletion write.
findings.evidence_excerpt: A **charge-edge** source-equal restart never writes the old candidate: it create-once closes the old intent `NOT_APPLIED`
findings.impact: After a crash before charge, the coordinator must either perform a durable pre-charge effect prohibited by the critical rule or cannot close the intent and re-prepare; treating the completion as implicitly allowed breaks the declared closed effect set and its evidence/accounting boundary.
findings.recommended_action: Add create-once NOT_APPLIED completion persistence as an explicit narrow uncharged pre-charge exception with exact owner, path, argv/effect, validation, accounting, and no-attempt/no-ledger-mutation invariants, or redesign restart so no extra pre-charge write is required.
